name: The Forgotten Court

stars.name: The Silent Judge
stars.notes: Cool white dwarf with featureless spectrum—no detectable absorption lines of any element. Surface temperature approximately 7,800 K. One of the oldest white dwarfs in the sector, nearly indistinguishable from background at long range.

planets.name: Witness
planets.notes: Dense, iron-rich world in close orbit. Surface bears extensive vitrification patterns—the entire planet was glazed by intense heat at some point in its history, likely during the star's red giant phase. Underneath the glass, radar detects hollow chambers.

planets.name: Verdict
planets.notes: Cold world with trace neon atmosphere. Surface is covered in a uniform layer of fine gray dust exactly 3.7 meters deep across the entire planet. Beneath the dust, the original terrain is pristine, as if the dust were deposited all at once.

planets.name: Sentence
planets.notes: Massive ice world at the system's edge. Interior generates anomalous thermal signature—warmer than it should be given its distance from the star. Source of heat is neither radioactive decay nor tidal forces. Origin unknown.

anomalies.name: The Uniform Dust
anomalies.notes: 3.7 meters of chemically identical fine gray dust covering the entire planetary surface to uniform depth. Composition is 60% silicon dioxide, 30% aluminum oxide, 10% unknown compound. The unknown compound does not occur naturally and matches no industrial process. Dust appears to have been deposited in a single event approximately 800 million years ago.

anomalies.name: The Warm Heart
anomalies.notes: Sentence's core temperature is approximately 340 K warmer than models predict. The excess heat is constant, does not fluctuate, and has no identifiable source. If artificial, it implies an energy source that has operated without maintenance for billions of years.

anomalies.name: The Vitrified Chambers
anomalies.location: Beneath the glass surface of Witness
anomalies.notes: Network of hollow chambers detected by ground-penetrating radar beneath Witness's vitrified surface. The glass layer sealed them when the star expanded into its red giant phase. Contents unknown—the glass is too thick and hard to penetrate with available equipment.

asteroid_belts.name: The Jury
asteroid_belts.notes: Metallic debris in unusually regular orbital spacing. Fragments show evidence of having once been a single large metallic structure rather than a natural body.

stations.name: Courthouse
stations.notes: Research station operated by the Anomaly Studies Division. Crew studies the Uniform Dust, the Warm Heart, and the Vitrified Chambers. The station's naming followed the system's juridical theme established by the discovery team.

faction_control.notes: The Division holds a research charter. A secondary claim by the Stellar Antiquities Institute focuses specifically on the Vitrified Chambers on Witness.

history: Catalogued in 2356 as a cooling white dwarf of minor astrophysical interest. The featureless spectrum of The Silent Judge drew brief academic attention before the system was deprioritized.

Rediscovered in 2487 when a mineral survey detected the anomalous thermal signature of Sentence. Follow-up investigation revealed the Uniform Dust on Verdict and the Vitrified Chambers on Witness, prompting the Anomaly Studies Division to establish Courthouse station in 2493.

Research over the past century has catalogued the anomalies in detail but explained none of them. The Uniform Dust's unknown compound, the Warm Heart's inexplicable energy source, and the sealed chambers beneath Witness's glass all resist analysis. A 2571 proposal to crack the glass on Witness was denied on preservation grounds.
description: The Forgotten Court is a system of sealed evidence and inexplicable verdicts. The Silent Judge—a dim, featureless white dwarf nearly ten billion years old—presides over three worlds, each bearing marks of intervention that defy natural explanation. Witness is glazed in a shell of glass hiding sealed chambers. Verdict is buried under a planet-wide layer of engineered dust. Sentence burns from within with a heat that has no source. The naming convention was the discovery team's dark joke, but it fits: this system feels like the aftermath of a judgment rendered by something with the power to reshape worlds.

Each anomaly is strange on its own. Together, they suggest a single intelligence operating across the entire system with capabilities that human science cannot replicate or explain. The Uniform Dust on Verdict was deposited in a single event—an entire planet coated in 3.7 meters of partially synthetic material simultaneously. The Warm Heart inside Sentence has been generating excess heat for billions of years without fuel or maintenance. The Vitrified Chambers on Witness were sealed not by intent but by stellar evolution, their builders apparently unconcerned that their star's expansion would entomb their work in glass. Either they planned to return and never did, or the glass was always part of the design.

Eighteen researchers at Courthouse station work to understand a system that resists understanding with elegant thoroughness. The dust does not match known chemistry. The heat does not match known physics. The chambers do not open. The Jury—the remnants of what may have been an artificial structure—orbits in pieces that tell nothing about their original form. The Forgotten Court keeps its own counsel, its Silent Judge offering no spectrum, no clue, no explanation. Whatever trial was held here ended long ago, and the verdict was never recorded in any language the living can read.
